Mild Steel Characteristics 
Mild steel belongs to the following category of low-carbon steel, with a small percentage of carbon, between 0. 05% and 0. 25%. This type of steel is highly ductile, making it easy to shape and weld. It's also cost-effective and easy to machine, so it's widely used in construction, automotive, and manufacturing industries.
Want to know more about mild steel?
Click here.
Properties-
Chemical Composition
Carbon (C): ≤ 0.25%
Manganese (Mn): 0.25% to 0.70%
Phosphorus (P): ≤ 0.05%
Sulfur (S): ≤ 0.05%
Other elements: Silicon (Si), Copper (Cu), Nickel (Ni), Chromium (Cr), etc.
Mechanical Properties 
Tensile Strength: Typically 330 - 540 MPa
Yield Strength: Typically 205 - 345 MPa
Elongation: 20% - 30%
Density 
Approximately 7.85 g/cm³
Quality assurance and material testing-
Mild steel pipes are subjected to thorough quality assurance and material testing, such as tensile strength, hardness, and impact tests. These tests ensure the pipes meet industry standards for durability and reliability, confirming their structural integrity and suitability for various uses. The quality checkers conducts different tests to check the quality of the MS Pipe. Some tests that are performed to check the quality of the product are-
Hardness test
Hydrostatic test
Intergranular corrosion test
Positive material identification
Ultrasonic test
In addition to quality tests, the quality checkers perform different inspections. These include third-party inspection and visual inspection. These are carried out by a third-party inspection team comprising well-regarded experts in the field. They possess extensive knowledge about the manufacturing of the pipes that will be supplied to the clients. These tests and inspections are conducted to ensure that the clients are satisfied with the products they receive.

Mild steel pipes have a wide range of applications across various industries due to their durability, versatility, and affordability. Here are some of the key applications of mild steel pipes:
Mild steel pipes are used in oil pipelines due to their low carbon content
Mild steel pipes are used in boiler tubes
MS black pipes are used in automotive exhaust systems
MS steel square pipes are used in structural purpose
MS Pipes uses in Water Supply Systems
Mild steel pipes are used in fuel pipelines
MS pipes are used in general building applications such as fencing, construction structure
Mild steel pipes are used in gas pipelines due to their high strength, resistance to corrosion
Mild steel round pipes are used in plumbing and water supply systems
